lessonsIntro: Putsborough's surf school runs from the beach itself, at the sheltered southern end of Woolacombe Bay.

text: Putsborough sits in the lee of Baggy Point, so it can still have rideable waves when other beaches are windy or rough. The beach describes itself as one of the safest in North Devon, which makes it a good place for a first lesson. Nick Thorn's two-hour sessions take beginners from age 6, and most people stand up within one or two sessions.

The beach's own advice is to stay clear of the rocks and surf to the right of the Yellow House. Don't go in unless you can swim 50 metres, wear a leash, stay no deeper than waist height while you're learning, and get out when you start to feel cold. We couldn't confirm RNLI lifeguard cover here, so treat a lesson as your safety net.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners to improvers
cards.text: One of North Devon's safer beaches, with a sandbar that helps improvers practise.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Windy days and winter
cards.text: Sheltered by Baggy Point, so it can have waves when other beaches are rough. Lessons and hire run year-round.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rocks at the southern end
cards.text: Keep away from the rocks and surf to the right of the Yellow House.

hireIntro: The surf centre on the beach hires boards and wetsuits, and Woolacombe village has more hire shops a short drive up the bay.

text: Start on a high-volume soft board, as Putsborough's own advice recommends lots of buoyancy for beginners. Improvers can move on to harder, more progressive boards from the surf centre. The sea here runs from about 15-18C in mid-August to 8-9C in early March. Wear a 3/2mm or 4/3mm in summer, and a 5/4mm or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood in early spring.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Buoyant soft board
cards.text: Soft beginner boards first, then harder progressive boards as you improve.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: Always wear one
cards.text: Beach rules say always wear a wetsuit: 3/2mm or 4/3mm in summer, 5/4mm or thicker in early spring.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: SUP on calm days
cards.text: Stand-up paddleboards can be hired from the surf centre. Always wear a leash.

shopsIntro: There's a beach shop and café at Putsborough, but no surf shop. Woolacombe village is the nearest place for surf kit.
shopsText: Putsborough has a beach shop and café by the car park, but for boards, wetsuits and accessories you need to head up the bay to Woolacombe. There, The Bay Surf Shop on Barton Road, Shore 2 Surf on West Road and Surfing Woolacombe on the beach slipway all sell surf gear.

lessons.q: What's the minimum age for lessons at Putsborough?
lessons.a: Nick Thorn coaches surfers aged 6 to 80.
Sessions last two hours and include a safety talk, equipment introduction and time in the water. Wetsuit and board are included.

lessons.q: Do I need to be able to swim?
lessons.a: Yes. The beach's own advice is not to surf unless you can swim at least 50 metres.

hire.q: What can I hire at Putsborough?
hire.a: The surf centre hires surfboards from soft beginner boards to harder boards, wetsuits and stand-up paddleboards.

hire.q: Where should I surf on a hire board?
hire.a: Stay away from the rocks and surf to the right of the Yellow House, keeping waist-deep while you learn.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop at Putsborough?
shops.a: No, only a beach shop and café. The nearest surf shops are in Woolacombe.
